contentFull:
Smart cameras reveal how broilers respond to heat stress and ageing 

A new study using advanced computer vision technology has shed fresh light on how broiler behaviour changes throughout the production cycle, offering poultry producers new tools to monitor welfare, detect problems early and manage heat stress more effectively.

Tony McDougalFreelance journalist

Aug 9

News

An AI-powered multi-camera system tracked broiler behaviour from 8 to 40 days of age, revealing changes linked to growth, welfare and heat stress. Photo: Boerderij

Researchers monitored 1,120 Ross 308 broilers across 4 production cycles using a multi-camera tracking system capable of following bird movements from 8-40 days of age. The technology automatically measured activity levels, feeding behaviour and drinking behaviour, providing an unprecedented picture of how broiler behaviour evolves as birds grow.

The findings confirm many observations familiar to poultry farmers, while also demonstrating how automated monitoring could transform the way welfare is assessed in commercial poultry houses.

One of the clearest conclusions was that age has a major impact on activity. As broilers grew, overall movement declined significantly. High-intensity activity, such as running, started falling as early as 15 days of age and declined more rapidly than lower-intensity movements. By around 30 days of age, activity levels across all categories were noticeably lower.

ALSO READ: Autochthonous breeds in a warming climate

According to the researchers, led by Professor Patricia Soster from the Department of Pathobiology, Pharmacology and Zoological Medicine, Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, at Ghent University, this reflects the biological reality of modern broilers. As bodyweight increases, movement becomes more physically demanding and birds naturally devote more energy to growth rather than locomotion. The results are consistent with previous research linking reduced activity in older birds to mobility challenges and poorer skeletal health.

For producers, this finding is important because activity may serve as an early warning signal. Significant deviations from expected activity patterns could indicate emerging welfare issues, including lameness, leg disorders or management problems.

Heat stress changes bird behaviour

The study also provided valuable insights into bird responses to heat stress. During periods when house temperatures reached approximately 29-30°C, birds spent significantly more time around drinkers and less time around feeders.

Overall activity levels were not significantly affected by the heat challenge. Instead of becoming dramatically less active, birds appeared to alter how they allocated their time, prioritising water consumption and reducing feeding activity.

This behavioural shift highlights a practical opportunity for poultry farmers. Monitoring drinker and feeder use may provide a more sensitive indicator of heat stress than activity levels alone. A sudden increase in drinking behaviour combined with fewer visits to feeders could serve as an early warning that birds are struggling to cope with rising temperatures.

ALSO READ: Poultry efficiency has come a long way and the progress is far from over

The research also showed that behaviour followed clear daily rhythms. Activity was generally highest during the morning and middle of the day before declining later. During heat-stress periods, feeding activity was suppressed while temperatures remained elevated but increased again during the evening once conditions returned to normal.

This finding is likely to resonate with producers who frequently observe birds compensating for reduced daytime feed intake by eating later in the day. The results reinforce the value of maintaining good environmental control and providing birds with opportunities to recover after periods of heat stress.

AI enables continuous welfare monitoring

Perhaps the most significant aspect of the work is the technology itself. The system used 4 cameras combined with artificial intelligence algorithms to track birds automatically. The researchers achieved a high level of tracking accuracy despite dramatic changes in bird size over the 6-week growing period.

Unlike traditional welfare assessments, which depend on periodic manual observations, automated systems can provide continuous monitoring without disturbing the flock. This creates opportunities to identify abnormal behavioural changes long before they become apparent through production performance or mortality figures.

ALSO READ: AI tracking reveals broiler behaviour throughout production

The researchers suggest that future precision livestock farming systems could alert farmers to potential welfare challenges, including heat stress, equipment failures, disease outbreaks and mobility problems. Sudden increases or decreases in activity, unusual feeding patterns or changes in drinker use could all provide early warnings.

There are still limitations. The work was conducted under experimental conditions at relatively low stocking densities, meaning additional validation is needed under commercial production conditions. The system also focused on only 3 behavioural measures and did not assess other welfare indicators such as dustbathing, panting or wing flapping.

Nevertheless, the study represents an important step forward in automated broiler monitoring. As poultry producers face growing pressure to demonstrate high welfare standards while maintaining efficiency, technologies capable of continuously measuring bird behaviour may become increasingly valuable.

The research, ‘Behavioral patterns in broiler chickens monitored with a multi-view tracking system’, is published on ScienceDirect and is available here.
translationZh:
一项采用先进计算机视觉技术的新研究揭示了肉鸡在整个生产周期中行为变化的规律，为家禽生产者提供了监测福利、早期发现问题以及更有效管理热应激的新工具。

研究人员利用AI驱动的多摄像头系统，在4个生产周期内监测了1,120只Ross 308肉鸡，该系统能够跟踪8至40日龄鸡只的活动。该技术自动测量了活动水平、采食行为和饮水行为，提供了肉鸡行为随生长变化的空前清晰的图景。

研究结果证实了家禽养殖户熟悉的许多观察，同时也展示了自动化监测如何能够改变商业禽舍中福利评估的方式。

最明确的结论之一是年龄对活动有重大影响。随着肉鸡生长，整体活动显著下降。高强度活动（如奔跑）早在15日龄就开始下降，且下降速度快于低强度活动。到约30日龄时，所有类别的活动水平都明显降低。

据研究人员称，这反映了现代肉鸡的生物学现实。随着体重增加，运动变得更加费力，鸡只自然将更多能量用于生长而非运动。这一结果与先前将老年鸡活动减少与行动能力下降和骨骼健康不佳联系起来的研究一致。

对生产者而言，这一发现很重要，因为活动水平可以作为早期预警信号。与预期活动模式的显著偏差可能表明出现了福利问题，包括跛行、腿部疾病或管理问题。

**热应激改变鸡只行为**

该研究还提供了对鸡只热应激反应的宝贵见解。在舍内温度达到约29-30°C的时期，鸡只在饮水器周围花费的时间显著增加，而在采食器周围的时间减少。

整体活动水平并未受到热应激挑战的显著影响。鸡只并未变得明显不活跃，而是改变了时间分配方式，优先饮水并减少采食活动。

这种行为转变凸显了家禽养殖户的一个实际机会。监测饮水和采食器的使用情况可能比单纯监测活动水平更能敏感地指示热应激。饮水行为突然增加，同时采食器访问次数减少，可以作为鸡只难以应对温度升高的早期预警。

研究还表明，行为遵循明显的昼夜节律。活动通常在早晨和中午最高，之后下降。在热应激期间，采食活动在温度持续升高时受到抑制，但在傍晚条件恢复正常后再次增加。

这一发现很可能引起生产者的共鸣，他们经常观察到鸡只通过在一天中较晚时间采食来补偿白天采食量减少的现象。结果强调了保持良好环境控制以及在热应激后为鸡只提供恢复机会的价值。

**AI实现连续福利监测**

这项工作中最重要的方面或许是技术本身。该系统使用4个摄像头结合人工智能算法自动跟踪鸡只。尽管鸡只在6周生长期内体型发生巨大变化，研究人员仍实现了高水平的跟踪精度。

与传统依赖定期人工观察的福利评估不同，自动化系统可以在不打扰鸡群的情况下提供连续监测。这为在异常行为变化通过生产性能或死亡率数据显现之前及早识别创造了机会。

研究人员建议，未来的精准畜牧业系统可以向养殖户发出潜在福利挑战的警报，包括热应激、设备故障、疾病爆发和行动问题。活动的突然增加或减少、异常的采食模式或饮水器使用变化都可能提供早期预警。

仍存在局限性。该研究是在实验条件下以相对较低的饲养密度进行的，这意味着需要在商业生产条件下进行额外验证。该系统还仅关注了3种行为指标，未评估其他福利指标，如沙浴、喘气或拍打翅膀。

尽管如此，该研究代表了自动化肉鸡监测的重要一步。随着家禽生产者面临展示高福利标准同时保持效率的压力日益增大，能够连续测量鸡只行为的技术可能变得越来越有价值。

这项名为“Behavioral patterns in broiler chickens monitored with a multi-view tracking system”的研究发表在ScienceDirect上，可在此处获取。
author: Tony McDougal
